title: Freeze runtime secret type and compatibility contract
body:
## Why / user outcome
Add a stable, reusable, typed runtime secret interface while preserving the existing `fleet secrets get/list` contract and its redaction guarantees. It must support in-memory application use without requiring a Fleet subprocess.

## Current evidence
At baseline commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs` has a name-only `Resolver`, `SecretSource`, `SecretValue`, and broker/BWS source chain. `fleet secrets` only dispatches `get` and `list` (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/secrets.rs`). `cargo test --locked -p fleet-secrets` passed 16 tests on 2026-11-12; these do not cover typed scopes or freshness policy.

## Scope / technical boundaries
Additive types in `fleet-secrets`: `SecretRef`, `SecretId`, `ProviderId`, `DataClass`, `ReadPolicy`, `ResolvedSecret`, redacted `SecretBytes`, and stable redacted error classes. Preserve the current resolver entry point and CLI behavior. This issue adds no writes, provider migration, PKI, or production operation.

## API and behavior
Design an async injectable `SecretStore` and `Resolver::resolve(&SecretRef, &ReadPolicy, CancellationToken) -> Result<ResolvedSecret, ResolveError>`; keep provider-specific capability descriptors explicit and source choice policy-driven. Secret bytes must not implement `Debug`, `Display`, or `Serialize`; callers reveal only via an explicit closure. Errors carry safe classes and no provider payload/stderr.

## Acceptance criteria
1. An in-memory fake adapter resolves a typed reference without spawning a process or touching disk/network.
2. Existing `fleet secrets get <name>` stdout, stderr, and exit behavior matches the pinned baseline fixtures exactly.
3. The new error enum distinguishes invalid reference, not found, unauthenticated, permission denied, unavailable, rate limit, unsupported, stale, conflict, malformed provider data, cancelled, timeout, partial, integrity, policy denied, and internal failures.
4. Provider choice is explicit; resolver does not try arbitrary providers merely because an earlier source failed.
5. Public result metadata can be rendered separately from secret bytes and remains redacted.

## Tests and oracle
Use pinned V1 CLI golden fixtures as compatibility oracle and an in-memory reference adapter as resolver oracle. Negative tests: `Debug` and serialization cannot expose secret bytes; empty/malformed values, ambiguous refs, policy-denied source, stale-forbidden result and cancelled request all fail with value-free errors. Include compile-time assertions that `SecretBytes` is not serializable.

## Security / environment
Synthetic values only. No live vault lookup, credential export or write. Keep names out of logs where they may be sensitive; provider errors must discard raw output.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157, requirement IDs V3-S02/S07/S13. V2, proposed High urgency 400, Backlog. No blocker. Enables ARCH-02/03/04 and forms a prerequisite for ARCH-06.

## Rollback / recovery
Additive API can be removed without migration while the old resolver remains. Do not remove or alter the V1 CLI semantics as part of rollback. No persistent data is written.

## Open decisions
Select async runtime and exact zeroization dependency only after workspace compatibility and maintenance review. Whether admin types share this crate or move later is deferred until a real consumer/build closure is measured.

title: Enforce freshness and safe cache invalidation in secrets broker
body:
## Why / user outcome
Prevent the secrets broker from silently returning rotated, revoked, or otherwise stale cached values after refresh failures. Retain a deliberate stale-while-revalidate option only when the caller's typed policy explicitly permits it.

## Current evidence
At `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs:532-546` serves any cached entry without checking age against request policy. Lines 280-293 retain old value and timestamp after an individual fetch failure or total outage. The #6767 work adds timestamp/source reporting and per-item refresh, but not a maximum serve age. Existing tests cover retained values and reported ages, not refusing stale reads.

## Scope / technical boundaries
Additive versioned/negotiated freshness metadata or endpoint, request-specific maximum age, explicit stale policy, and keyed invalidation on successful write. Preserve old clients by negotiation or additive wire shape; do not silently change empty-value meaning. This issue is code plus synthetic tests only; no production vault writes or rotations.

## API / behavior
Broker read response identifies source, revision if available, fetch time/age, and stale state. For stale-forbidden requests, return a typed stale/unavailable status without value. For stale-allowed requests, return value only within caller's maximum stale duration and mark it stale. Successful mutation invalidates the relevant cache key; refresh success must not freshen entries whose own fetch failed.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Fake-clock request older than max age is refused in stale-forbidden mode.
2. Explicit stale-allowed request returns the value and exact age/stale metadata only if within its configured bound.
3. Invalidation immediately removes one named entry; unrelated entries remain unchanged.
4. Failed per-item and whole-cache refresh preserve original timestamp and do not grant extra freshness.
5. Metrics count stale serves/refusals and invalidations without secret values or sensitive names.
6. Legacy client fixture still parses the version-1 response or fails closed with a documented negotiation response.

## Tests and oracle
Use a fake clock and a small freshness state model as oracle; model outcomes are ServeFresh, ServeStaleExplicitly, or Refuse. Negative cases: rotated value plus failing BWS get; revoked value; total outage past max age; a future timestamp/clock rollback; partial pagination; an attempted invalidation of a different key. Assert stale-forbidden responses never include the value.

## Security / environment
All values and provider responses are synthetic. Never call BWS, OP, or broker production endpoint in tests.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157; V2, proposed High urgency 450, Backlog. Depends on ARCH-01's `ReadPolicy`; blocks admin writes and any future live rotation.

## Rollback / recovery
Retain wire compatibility. If new policy metadata is unavailable, fail closed for freshness-sensitive reads rather than returning old cached values indefinitely. Roll back server capability only while the consumer path remains fail-closed; preserve diagnostic age metadata.

## Open decisions
Select default max ages by data class after benchmark and threat review. Confirm how existing clients negotiate without changing their current get/list semantics.

title: Add capability-described read adapters and synthetic benchmark harness
body:
## Why / user outcome
Measure current Fleet broker/resolver and evaluate provider paths with repeatable synthetic workloads. Expose actual provider capabilities and distinguish unsupported operations from denied permissions, empty results, and transient failures.

## Current evidence
`fleet-secrets` currently uses broker transport and `bws` CLI fallback, and has no OP/BW adapter. Broker makes a list then individual gets with eight worker threads (`fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs`). No benchmark harness or measured performance baseline was found in the inspected Fleet workspace at commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`.

## Scope / technical boundaries
Implement capability descriptors and read-only adapters first for existing BWS path and separately authorized/synthetic OP path. Keep `bw` distinct from `bws`; do not infer its permission or enable personal-vault inventory. Investigate fnox's public Rust API and maturity before adoption; no subprocess integration solely for parity. Benchmark cold/warm get, list/page, batch, startup, auth overhead, concurrency, failures, p50/p95/p99, throughput, RSS and rate limits.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Capability report states adapter/version, supported operations/fields, pagination, revision/CAS support and observed permission status separately.
2. Synthetic benchmark records provider, host, version, fixture, concurrency, sample count and quantiles with secrets excluded.
3. Report compares resolver, broker, direct adapter/CLI where supported, plus fnox only after API evidence.
4. A denied read is never normalized to not-found; partial pagination is marked incomplete.
5. Batch resolution preserves input order and reports per-item outcomes while bounding concurrency.

## Tests and oracle
Adapter conformance tests against a known in-memory synthetic provider and hand-authored capability fixture are the oracle. Negative tests: 403, 429/Retry-After, auth failure, truncated page, malformed record, unsupported list/write, and BWS configured without any BW credential. Verify outputs/logs contain no secret value or token.

## Security / environment
Use isolated synthetic vaults only; no real credential benchmark or raw output. `bw` tests remain disabled until separately authorized. Provider documentation and API claims must cite dated primary-source results in the research issue.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157; V2, proposed High urgency 400, Backlog. Depends on ARCH-01 and ARCH-02; provider adoption itself remains gated by source review and synthetic evidence.

## Rollback / recovery
Feature-gate each adapter, default off. Remove a candidate adapter without changing the BWS compatibility fallback. Benchmark output is nonsecret report data and can be discarded/recomputed.

## Open decisions
Official SDK versus CLI adapter choice, OP service account scope, and fnox API stability require current upstream/API evidence and measurement.

title: Define canonical credential mapping and per-item replication policy
body:
## Why / user outcome
Provide a lossless, provider-neutral credential model that preserves logical identity, native IDs/revisions, typed fields, classification, provenance and explicit replication rules without conflating BWS, Bitwarden Password Manager, and 1Password.

## Current evidence
At baseline commit `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, current `fleet-secrets` only resolves a named string and does not store canonical credential objects or provider mappings. No generic provider write model exists.

## Scope / technical boundaries
Specify schema/versioning for `Credential`, `SecretField`, field type/order, stable logical ID, per-provider native ID/revision, tags, provenance, security class, scope/compartment, replica policy and encrypted lossless sidecar. Keep canonical types in `fleet-secrets` initially; do not create a crate solely for types. No provider write or migration in this issue.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Synthetic OP/BWS-compatible fixtures round-trip every supported field and unknown sidecar without loss.
2. Field-level compare reports equal, source-only change, target-only change, conflict, missing, and unsupported distinctly.
3. Update mapping preserves native original item ID and represents revisions/conditional write capability.
4. Policy explain separates read, write, replicate, export and recovery permission.
5. RootPrivate/Recovery defaults deny general mirroring; compartments are provider-specific unless an explicit policy authorizes replication.
6. Schema version migration is deterministic and preserves unknown fields.

## Tests and oracle
Use a versioned canonical JSON golden corpus and round-trip property tests as oracle. Negative tests: duplicate aliases, unknown field without sidecar, unsupported native field, conflicting aliases, root private in default shared scope, and policy that authorizes read but not export. Assert no timestamp-only conflict resolution.

## Security / environment
Synthetic data only. Do not access personal vaults or export private keys. Metadata itself may be sensitive; fixtures must be fabricated.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157; V2-to-V3, proposed High urgency 400, Backlog. Depends on ARCH-01 and ARCH-03. Enables ARCH-05 and ARCH-08. `bw` access remains separately approval-blocked.

## Rollback / recovery
No persistent production data or migration. Versioned parser can retain old schema reader; if lossless sidecar cannot be proven, refuse write planning rather than discard provider fields.

## Open decisions
Finalize field registry only after provider capability probes; decide sidecar envelope and metadata storage after threat model.

title: Build plan/apply/recover reconciliation and nonsecret operation journal
body:
## Why / user outcome
Reconcile two provider inventories safely from a verified baseline, preserving native item identity and both sides of conflicts while making partial mutation recoverable.

## Current evidence
No canonical inventory, three-way sync engine, `zz.delete` lifecycle, or secrets journal was found in the inspected Fleet workspace at `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`. `fleet-queue` has a durable GitHub creation outbox, but that is for issue/PR/comment creation and is not a secret event journal or transaction engine (`creation_outbox.rs`).

## Scope / technical boundaries
Implement deterministic plan generation, revision-bound approval, staged/idempotent write saga, read-back verification, nonsecret append-only journal, resume/recovery and protected `zz.delete` history over fake providers. Keep writer capability in an optional admin module/crate, separate from runtime reads. No live reconciliation in this ticket.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Plan records scope, baseline, revisions, per-field actions, conflicts, source/destination and digest; plan command causes zero writes.
2. Apply requires scope-matched approval and each operation has idempotency key and precondition.
3. Completion requires provider read-back proof; partial result is `Partial/Uncertain`, never reported as atomic success.
4. Same-field concurrent changes preserve both and require resolution; no timestamps silently choose.
5. An update targets the original native ID; stale-password path stores verified protected `zz.delete` history before update.
6. Journal and metadata contain no secret plaintext, raw provider token, low-entropy unkeyed comparison, or private key bytes.
7. Resume resolves a prior uncertain write by read-back/idempotency before any retry.

## Tests and oracle
Build a model-based reference merge/state machine and generate operation sequences; compare implementation state against model after every action. Inject crash before/after each provider write, timeout, 403, partial list, rate limit, readback mismatch, and cancellation. Negative tests: outage/permission/pagination cannot imply delete; false-delete is impossible; journal inspection shows no payload.

## Security / environment
Synthetic adapters/fixtures only. Production first sweep, password rotation, tombstone creation in real providers, or live provider writes are not authorized and require separate approval.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157; V3, proposed High urgency 450, Backlog. Depends on ARCH-02 and ARCH-04; requires ARCH-03 provider capability/write tests before adapter-specific integration.

## Rollback / recovery
Pause future applies, retain journal and plan digest, then resume or run documented compensation per receipt. Never erase completed history or claim a cross-provider atomic rollback. Existing GitHub issue creation outbox is not reused.

## Open decisions
Choose journal storage/encryption and retention only after an independent bootstrap/recovery review. Production scope stays blocked pending explicit go/no-go.

title: Add crypto signer contracts and synthetic PKI engine
body:
## Why / user outcome
Create an importable PKI library and abstract signer seam usable in memory and by CLI without invoking the CLI internally. Validate the required reference graph with synthetic keys and explicit algorithm/client capability policy.

## Current evidence
No `cert`/`pki`, `generate`, crypto provider, signer, or PKI crate/domain is present in the Fleet registry/workspace at baseline `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`. The Iroh key in `pkgs/id` is an endpoint identity and is not an X.509 signer abstraction. Existing `fleet-connect` binary must stay within its 2 MiB hard gate.

## Scope / technical boundaries
Design `Signer`, `KeyResolver`, policy-driven algorithm registry, profile-based root/issuer/leaf/chain/CRL models, artifact sink and in-memory flow. Implement synthetic four-root identities, nine asymmetric root cross-certificates, Base and Internal Web issuer sets with A/B partitions and eligible direct cross-signs; preserve roots-only as supported alternative. ML-DSA-44 is baseline, RSA-4096 production and RSA-2048 long-root compatibility requires explicit policy. Do not build CA server or publish DNS.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Generated graph is validated by independent verifier and matches count/identity relationships in source: 20 CA key pairs and 65 CA certs excluding leaves.
2. A memory sink works without files, subprocesses, or network.
3. PQ-only trust rejects any classical certificate path; target lacking ML-DSA capability is reported unsupported and not silently substituted.
4. Explicit policy rejects long-lived RSA-2048 root; renewal with same key does not rotate key identity.
5. OCSP extension is absent when no verified responder is available; unsupported ML-DSA OCSP is reported.
6. Public/private artifact classification requires an authorized sink for private output.

## Tests and oracle
Use a reference chain graph/model plus independent OpenSSL and independent Rust verifier versions pinned in test evidence. Negative tests: classical root/leaf in PQ-only chain, malformed OID/extension, expired/not-yet-valid cert, disallowed algorithm, unsupported protocol output, and accidental private-key serialization.

## Security / environment
Synthetic keys and local test fixtures only. This issue does not authorize generating or exporting production root keys or changing trust stores.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157; V3, proposed High urgency 450, Backlog. Depends on ARCH-01 and crypto backend research; no dependency on live custody, OpenBao, or secret-store writes.

## Rollback / recovery
Keep new crypto/PKI features opt-in; old builds and connect artifact remain unchanged. Remove candidate algorithm feature without changing serialized public manifest format. Do not discard existing trust artifacts if implementation is later rolled back.

## Open decisions
Select Rust crypto/X.509 libraries after current primary-source retrieval and interoperability proof, especially ML-DSA support.

title: Integrate capabilities and feature profiles into Fleet multicall
body:
## Why / user outcome
Expose added secrets, generation and certificate capabilities through the existing Fleet multicall registry and one CLI, with help that accurately distinguishes compiled, invocation-profile and configuration-enabled features. Do not ship a competing CLI.

## Current evidence
`fleet-registry` is std-only and tracks compiled/profile/effective capability sets. Existing variants are full, serve and connect; connect is proxy-client only and hard-capped at 2 MiB stripped. No cert/pki or generate domain exists. `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/Cargo.toml` currently feature-gates command groups.

## Scope / technical boundaries
Add registry entries and command feature gates for typed secrets/runtime, optional admin, crypto/PKI, generation and formats. Proposed profiles: consumer-min, agent, existing fleet, admin, serve. Keep names/profile semantics compatible and generated help/schema sourced from one registry. No unrelated PM Stack or queue behavior changes.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Test matrix enumerates compiled, invocation-profile and effective capabilities for each shipped variant.
2. Missing commands render existing registry-style unavailable response, rather than parser failure or silent omission.
3. Every command's JSON help schema and plain help agree on prerequisites and unavailable features.
4. Existing fleet get/list behavior and exit codes remain unchanged.
5. `fleet-connect` does not link secrets/crypto/PKI dependencies and its final stripped artifact remains ≤2 MiB.
6. New consumer-min and agent sizes and startup are measured against proposed budgets and documented; budgets are not called passed until measured.

## Tests and oracle
Capability golden matrix and executable smoke tests are the oracle. Negative tests: invocation alias cannot widen compiled capabilities; connect cannot run `cert`/`secrets`; configuration-disabled feature refuses operation; aliases map to identical typed request, not divergent behavior. Nix final artifact size gate is required.

## Security / environment
No live secrets or production signing. Build and test only; no package deployment.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157; V2-to-V3, proposed High urgency 400, Backlog. Depends on ARCH-01/06; admin feature requires ARCH-05 before inclusion. Coordinate separately with binary/profile owner.

## Rollback / recovery
Revert additive feature selections/registry entries and retain old variants; verify connect budget and aliases after rollback. Keep CLI compatibility fixtures as guard.

## Open decisions
Approve proposed consumer-min/agent targets only after baseline builds; decide whether profiles map to extra Nix artifacts or Cargo feature sets.

title: Specify root custody, three-destination escrow, and recovery proof
body:
## Why / user outcome
Define how initial root private keys are separated into active signing and encrypted escrow, recovered independently, and later migrated to offline/hardware signing. The addendum names three initial destinations: encrypted laptop storage, authorized BWS project, and authorized 1Password vault.

## Current evidence
No Fleet root-key custody model or CA code exists at baseline `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`. Current Iroh identity export/import is a separate application-specific encrypted envelope, not a reusable root-escrow policy. No actual production permissions or vault destinations were verified by this census.

## Scope / technical boundaries
Produce threat model, custody manifest, failure/compromise graph, recovery sequence and synthetic archive/restore proof. Assess SOPS/age recipients and complete bundle versus individually recoverable root archives. Evaluate Cloudflare R2 only as researched client-side-encrypted possible extra location; it is not an automatically enabled fourth replica. Preserve future offline/HSM migration.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Manifest distinguishes active signer handle from escrow object and records root identity/generation, fingerprint, archive version, destination, integrity verification and restore evidence.
2. Synthetic bundle restores using a recovery identity stored separately from both archive and source repository.
3. Threat/failure graph states which host/vendor/auth/network losses each copy survives and identifies shared failure domains.
4. Default secret replication and cache cannot copy RootPrivate; explicit custody policy is separately required.
5. Three named destinations and their separate verification obligations are stated; R2 remains research until another decision.
6. Document includes offline/HSM transition and avoids circular dependency on the root being recovered.

## Tests and oracle
Use an isolated synthetic key and restore exercise as executable oracle; compare restored public fingerprint with original. Negative cases: wrong recovery identity, archive tamper, missing destination receipt, private key in general replication plan, recovery key stored alongside archive, and three same-host OpenBao containers labelled as independent HA.

## Security / environment
No production key creation, export, upload, synchronization, or root signing. Those actions require separate explicit approval and reviewed rollback/custody gates. No real vault data.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157; V3, proposed High urgency 450, Backlog for design/synthetic work. Depends on ARCH-04/05/06. Production operations are separately lifecycle `Blocked` pending authorization; this issue itself must not perform them.

## Rollback / recovery
If synthetic recovery fails, stop and revise design; do not remove existing copies or infer lossless restore. For future production, rollback means stopping new replication while retaining last verified copies and receipts.

## Open decisions
Locations/identities for independent age recovery recipients and exact access scopes require operator decision. Verify permissions before any production use.

title: Research federation, fnox, OpenBao, SOPS/age, and workload identity hooks
body:
## Why / user outcome
Create falsifiable, source-backed decisions for eventual federation and identity without making speculative infrastructure a dependency of current secret/PKI work. Preserve independent providers and per-credential policy rather than universal replication.

## Current evidence
At baseline `34faffbff26615e313488f6d04705a444342e41e`, no Fleet fnox/OpenBao/SecureStore/SOPS provider or federation module was found. The current architecture has a broker cache and name-based BWS resolver only. No current public vendor documentation has been fetched for this proposal; source review and dated evidence are mandatory work in the research issue.

## Scope / technical boundaries
Research primary sources and evaluate fnox Rust API/stability/adapters/cache/injection; SOPS/age and existing NixOS bootstrap; SecureStore crypto/format/maintenance versus age; OpenBao KV/dynamic/PKI/SSH/Transit/auth/audit and deployment/failure domains; R2/client-side encryption; SPIFFE/SPIRE, Kubernetes operators and cross-system responsibility. Define interface hooks and go/no-go criteria. No deploy, provider enablement, or live secret migration.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Each candidate includes dated primary-source links, version/API claims, capability/permission matrix, maintenance evidence, alternatives, threat model, costs and a measurable go/no-go.
2. OpenBao stages distinguish local lab from independent failure domains; same-host containers cannot be described as HA.
3. Federation model describes compartment, preferred source, consistency/version/freshness, failure behavior and compromise expansion per credential class.
4. Dynamic/short-lived credentials cannot be treated as static passwords in ordinary replication.
5. fnox adoption requires a documented embedded API versus executable decision and benchmark comparison; no assumption of universal write support.
6. SOPS/age private identities remain outside Git/Nix store; SecureStore must establish an advantage before adding a format.
7. Research concludes independently and cannot block current V2/V3 baseline.

## Tests and oracle
Use a documented failure/compromise graph and a local synthetic lab experiment where applicable; each research claim must point to retrieved source text/date or explicitly say unverified. Negative cases: vendor outage does not authorize stale read without policy; shared authentication dependency is not independent; same-host nodes are one failure domain; root copies do not automatically expand to R2 or every future provider.

## Security / environment
Public research and isolated synthetic lab only. No secrets, production provider writes, cloud resource creation, or service deployment.

## Dependencies / priority / stage
Parent #9157; V4 nonblocking, proposed Standard urgency 200, Backlog. Depends on ARCH-01/02/04 for stable contract and policy context; does not block PKI or secrets-core milestones.

## Rollback / recovery
Research can be parked or superseded without code/data migration. No infrastructure is enabled by its completion. Preserve decision record and source access date so claims can be refreshed.

## Open decisions
Actual hosting locations, provider scopes, workloads, and tolerance for per-class offline staleness remain operator decisions.
